newsitem.title: UK: Boots disappointed by OFT rule on OTC drugs.
newsitem.headline: Boots disappointed by OFT rule on OTC drugs.

text.p: British chemist and retail chain Boots Plc said it was disappointed that the Office of Fair Trading had decided to move to stop Resale Price Maintenance (RPM) on non-prescription medicines.
"We firmly believe that RPM operates in the public interest and that this will be the conclusion of the Restrictive Practices Court in due course," a statement from the company said.
The OFT director general John Bridgeman said earlier on Friday that he would ask the RPC for leave to apply to lift legislation allowing RPM on over-the-counter medicines.
Boots has not reduced prices of OTC medicines during the inquiry into pricing and industry observers said it was unlikely to take that route in the near future.
Superdrug, Kingfisher Plc's high street drugstore chain, meanwhile welcomed the OFT's decision but said it would not be instigating immediate price cuts.

"The OFT has effectively sounded the death knell of RPM and while we are not in favour of waiting for the RPC to rule, which may not be for two years, this is a complex area requiring considered decisions," a statement from Superdrug said.
